covering.note: Unlike most tortoises, its shell bends when pressed.

size.note: Its shell grows to about 18 cm long, and it rarely weighs more than 500 g.

diet.note: It eats herbs, succulent plants and flowers, plus the odd beetle.

activity.note: It comes out to feed in the early morning.

young.note: A female lays one large egg a year, rarely two.

lifespan.note: Pancake tortoises have lived more than 25 years in zoos.

clues.text: Its shell is so flat it looks like a pancake.
It lives on rocky hills called kopjes that rise out of the savanna.
It hides in narrow cracks between and under slabs of rock.
It is a good climber: some have been found in cracks high up on tall boulders.
Main threats: collecting for the pet trade, and breaking up the rocks it hides in.
International trade in it has been controlled since 1975 (CITES Appendix II).

facts.text: Its shell is soft and bendy because the bones underneath have open gaps. That lets it squeeze into narrow cracks.
Collecting and habitat damage cut its numbers by about 80% in 30 years.
In Kenya, about 95% of pancake tortoises live outside protected areas.
It keeps to a small home area and returns to the same rock cracks again and again.
The egg is laid at the start of the rainy season. Hatchlings are 3 to 5 cm long.
It takes 5 to 9 years to grow up.
Collectors sometimes pry apart the rocks it hides in, destroying the cracks it needs.
